title: two-phase-otel-upload-idempotency-shim-for-tempo-writes
creator: Ava Chen
description:
Problem: When bridging OpenTelemetry (OTLP) HTTP/protobuf ingestion to Tempo's gRPC ingest we occasionally observe duplicated spans and partial-batch replays after transient failures. Root causes include lack of a consistent batch id across client retries, non-atomic handoff between HTTP receiver and backend writer, and retry semantics that re-send compressed batches without an idempotency token.

Goal: Add a lightweight two-phase upload shim that provides idempotent, resumable handoff semantics for OTLP->Tempo writes. The shim should introduce a minimal prewrite/commit protocol (batch reservation + commit/ack) and durable metadata for short-lived retries, integrate with our existing OTLP receiver, and be safe to deploy behind our existing ingress and buffering layers. The feature must be covered by a golden-backend integration test harness that can inject failures (connection drops, partial responses, duplicate retries) to validate duplication reduction and performance overheads.

Scope out-of-band: This ticket focuses on the shim and integration tests; schema translation and long-term archival of uncommitted batches is out-of-scope and will be tracked separately.
acceptance_criteria: Shim accepts OTLP HTTP/protobuf v0.17+ and exposes Tempo-compatible gRPC writes with a two-phase commit handshake.
Synthetic replay tests show >=99% reduction in duplicate spans compared to current bridge behavior for injected transient failures.
Integration test harness (GitHub Actions) with golden traces and failure-injection scenarios added and passing on CI.
Runtime overhead measured: additional memory per active batch < 3MB and P95 latency increase for steady-state write path < 12% under p50 traffic profile.
Monitoring: new Prometheus metrics (batch_reservations, reservation_age_seconds, commit_rate, duplicate_detected) instrumented and dashboards created in Grafana.
Rollout plan documented (canary percentage, fallback toggle, rollback steps) and validated with one internal team prior to full rollout.
tasks: Design protocol doc for two-phase OTLP prewrite/commit (concurrency model, idempotency key format, TTL semantics).
Prototype in Golang as a shim component that sits between HTTP receiver and backend writer (in-memory reservation store + optional Redis spill).
Add idempotency key propagation to OTLP receiver path and unit tests for key generation and validation.
Implement commit path that performs Tempo gRPC write and acknowledges reservation; implement safe retry semantics for commit responses.
Build integration test harness: golden trace dataset, failure injection scripts (tcp drop, grpc abort, partial ack), and performance regression tests.
Add Prometheus metrics and Grafana dashboard panels; create alert thresholds for reservation-age and duplicate detections.
Prepare rollout plan, feature flag, migration notes, and runbook for incidents.
Create PR, iterate on review feedback, and perform canary with observability team.

notes:
Design trade-offs:
- Use short-lived reservation metadata (TTL 60s default) to avoid unbounded state; this trades off risk of losing reservation vs having a small risk of transient duplicate if reservation expired.
- Storage: Redis preferred for durability and cross-instance visibility; fallback local disk for single-node canary to reduce infra changes.
- Idempotency key format: versioned token 'v1:<region>:<timestamp>:<uuid>' to allow future protocol upgrades and debugability.
- Testing: focus first on replay/duplication and not on long-term archival or analytics of uncommitted batches (tracked separately).
